issues.legal_issue: Delegating authority to set a municipal property-tax rate without prescribing a maximum rate is not excessive when the governing statutory scheme provides sufficient policy, guidance, and control.
material_facts: The statutory scheme did not prescribe a maximum rate for the relevant property tax.
The tax could be levied only for purposes authorized by the governing law, and receipts and spending were restricted to municipal purposes and budgetary controls.
The rate was determined by an elected municipal body accountable to the people, after consideration and adoption of annual budget estimates.
The legislature retained power to alter the delegation, and the scheme provided controls over municipal rules and expenditure.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a statutory maximum rate did not make the delegation of taxing power excessive or arbitrary.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principle that fixing a tax rate may be delegated where the statute provides policy or guidance and the delegation is controlled by the statutory scheme. It relied on the purposes-of-the-Act principle in Western India Theatres Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of the City of Poona, the delegation principles in Pandit Banarsi Das Bhanot v. Madhya Pradesh, and Corporation of Calcutta v. Liberty Cinema. It considered Devi Das v. Punjab and followed the guidance analysis in Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Birla Mills. The court examined ss. 127 and 129, the budget and municipal-fund controls in ss. 82, 86, 88, 89, and 95–100, and the rule-making controls in ss. 454–457 of the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act. It also noted the legislature’s power to impose a maximum rate, which it later exercised.

rule.if: municipal_tax_rate_delegation_case and tax_restricted_to_authorized_purposes and elected_taxing_body_accountable and municipal_funds_and_budgets_controlled

predicates.municipal_tax_rate_delegation_case: The proceeding challenges the delegation of authority to set a rate of municipal tax.
predicates.tax_restricted_to_authorized_purposes: The law restricts the tax to purposes authorized for the municipality.
predicates.elected_taxing_body_accountable: An elected municipal body responsible to the people sets the tax rate.
predicates.municipal_funds_and_budgets_controlled: The law subjects municipal receipts and expenditure to fund and budget controls.

issues.definition: When a municipal tax-rate delegation is limited to authorized purposes and exercised by an accountable body under fund and budget controls, the delegation is not excessive.

issues.legal_issue: A municipal property-tax assessment is not invalid merely because the commissioner maintains one assessment book for the whole municipal area instead of separate ward assessment books.
material_facts: The commissioner maintained one assessment book for the municipal area.
The taxation rule expressly allowed the commissioner to choose between one assessment book and separate ward assessment books.
Other rules referred to ward assessment books when providing for public notice, inspection, complaints, and authentication.

The statutory scheme provided for notice and opportunities to inspect and complain, and the court found that treating those protections as applicable only when ward books were kept would create anomalies.
issues.conclusion: The assessment book was valid, and the bills and demand notices could not be challenged solely because one book, rather than separate ward books, was maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The court construed r. 10 of the Taxation Rules as permissive, relying on its language and the deliberate departure from s. 157 of the Bombay Municipal Corporation Act, 1888. It read rr. 13, 15, and 19 consistently with the option in r. 10, reasoning that their references to ward assessment books could not sensibly deprive ratepayers of notice, inspection, or complaint rights when one book was used. It also reasoned that authentication under r. 19 gave the tax entry a limited evidentiary conclusiveness and was not a basis for making one-book assessments invalid.

predicates.challenge_to_municipal_property_tax_asse: The proceeding challenges a municipal property-tax assessment or the resulting bills and demand notices.
predicates.commissioner_maintained_one_assessment_b: The commissioner maintained one assessment book for the municipal area rather than separate books for each ward.
predicates.governing_rule_allows_one_book_or_ward_b: The governing rule gives the commissioner a choice between one assessment book and separate ward assessment books.

issues.definition: When a property-tax assessment is challenged because the commissioner used one book and the governing rule permits that choice, the single-book assessment is valid.

issues.legal_issue: A taxpayer’s liability for municipal property tax arises from the completed tax entry in the assessment book and does not depend on authentication of that book.
material_facts: The assessment process required the tax amount to be entered after the tax rates were fixed, the complaint period had expired, and any complaints had been decided.
The rules provided for authentication of the assessment book after those entries were completed.
The court treated authentication as serving a limited evidentiary purpose rather than as the event that created liability.
issues.conclusion: Liability to pay the property tax arises from the prescribed tax entry and is not dependent on authentication of the assessment book.
issues.legal_principle: Applying rr. 9(e) and 30 of the Taxation Rules, the court held that liability arises when the tax amount is entered following the prescribed assessment and complaint process. Authentication under r. 19 makes the entry conclusive evidence for the limited purpose of enabling demands to be issued; it is not a condition for the accrual of liability.

predicates.municipal_property_tax_assessment_case: The proceeding concerns liability for municipal property tax assessed through an assessment book.
predicates.tax_amount_entered_after_rate_and_compla: The tax amount was entered after the rate was fixed, the complaint period ended, and any complaints were resolved.

issues.definition: When the prescribed tax amount has been entered after the rate and complaint process, liability does not depend on later authentication of the assessment book.
